facility_roles.quote: For the past decade, the BICEP/Keck collaboration has been operating a series of telescopes at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station

intervals.label: observations
intervals.note: The first (30/40 GHz) receiver started observing in early 2020 (also "since 2020", LAMBDA); further receivers were added later. The official BICEP/Keck publication list (checked 2026-10-26) includes a 2026 SPIE paper titled "Optical characterization of the BICEP Array 150 and 220/270 GHz CMB polarimeters in the 2026 season".
intervals.quote: The 30/40 GHz receiver is designed to constrain the synchrotron foreground and has begun observing at the South Pole in early 2020.

physics_goals.quote: The BICEP Array telescope is a set of multi-frequency cameras designed to constrain the energy scale of inflation through CMB B-mode searches while also controlling the polarized galactic foregrounds.
physics_goals.value: Constrain the energy scale of inflation through CMB B-mode searches while controlling polarized galactic foregrounds.

summary.plain: The newest BICEP/Keck telescope at the South Pole: four refracting telescopes in six frequency bands, built to detect or limit the polarization pattern left by gravitational waves from inflation while subtracting galactic foregrounds.
summary.technical: Stage-3 BICEP/Keck instrument: four BICEP3-class 550 mm receivers at 30/40, 95, 150 and 220/270 GHz, >30,000 detectors, projected sigma(r) ~ 0.003; first receiver observing since early 2020; replaced the Keck Array in late 2019.
